findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it is never used as a guard
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer looks for methods named `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) to decide whether to include an attribute in the output. The method is defined as `include_website_name` without the `?`, so it is just a regular method that is never invoked by the serialization framework. As a result, `website_name` will always be serialized even when `website` is blank, potentially outputting `nil` or causing unexpected behavior.

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking website info for TL0 users
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105–111) includes `:website` so that it is hidden from anonymous viewers when the profile belongs to a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?` returns true). However, `:website_name` is not in that list, so even when `website` is suppressed for untrusted users, `website_name` will still be serialized and exposed, effectively leaking the same information that `untrusted_attributes` is meant to protect. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` or its include guard should also check `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: Subdomain comparison logic fails for certain domain structures (e.g., co.uk TLDs)
findings.body: The heuristic on line 144 compares `website_host.split('.')[1..-1]` with `discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` when both have the same number of dot-separated parts and more than 2 parts. For domains like `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.example.co.uk`, this would compare `example.co.uk` with `example.co.uk` and incorrectly treat them as the same base domain (which happens to be correct here), but for `www.example.co.uk` vs `forum.other.co.uk` it would compare `example.co.uk` with `other.co.uk` and correctly reject. However, for a case like `sub.domain.com` vs `other.domain.com` where the actual registrable domains differ but share a TLD, the logic may produce unexpected results. More critically, the `else` branch (line 149) only checks if `discourse_host` ends with `website_host`, not the reverse, so `www.example.com` as the website with `example.com` as the instance host would not match, even though they share the same registrable domain.
